tips.comment: Estrange would not mind a bit of rain but won comfortably over course and distance on good in a Group 3 race in May and now goes for a repeat performance in a Group 2 that has only attracted three opponents.

Winner over a longer trip at York last time out in a Group Three. Today's quick ground looks ideal and looks capable of landing the double here in this small field, in what could turn into a sprint up the long home straight here at Haydock.

Sir Lowrys Pass did all his best work late on at Redcar in the competitive Zetland Gold Cup last time. Ultimately a little unlucky there. Step up to 1m4f likely to suit. Well bred by Siyouni out of a Galileo mare. Progressive and unexposed sort with two wins from six races so far. Odds on the short side for a big field handicap but the way this 4yo colt finished his last race suggests he can win races off this mark. Ed Walker having a great season. Paul Mulrennan replaces the jockey from that last race. Big shout.

The price of this one doesn't make any sense to me and has to be the e/w value at 20/1. He was the outsider of 3 when winning easily last time out, which isn't the usual prep for a race this competitive. But that was his first attempt at this trip, and the 6lb rise has been partially offset by booking a decent 3lb claiming apprentice. He got within half a length of a future listed winner in a novice race, and he's bred to be decent, so is surely worth a little e/w money here.
Backing this gelding each way alongside Sol Cayo. They're drawn on either side. He matches the profile of a few previous winners, and he's a huge price.

A quick turnaround for Intrusively, and with Photosynthesis's trainer not amongst the winners recently, the answer could be Northern Express, who has won off 2lb higher and was probably highly tried at Ascot last time.

For a horse with as much ability as Jumby, the 14/1 on offer looks like a very tempting each way price. He had been mixing it in Pattern races in his younger days; however, he probably isn't up to that grade now. His rating has dropped to a mark where he could be competitive in races like this. The stable is in good form and must be respected given the manner in which the runners are placed.

Interesting. They raced in group races recently, so they clearly hold this horse in high regard. Drops back into a handicap today, and although conceding weight all round, should give a good account for top connections.

Since switching to faster ground has done nothing but improve, going on a 3x win streak, with that coming to an end at York with an unfavorable draw but still finishing 3 lengths off the winner. Could still have room for more progress, drawn well here and drops 1 lb off last run that still seems a workable mark. Yard is in good nick and doesn't often send horses here. Jason Hart booked, who's a profitable pairing for this yard.
Dc Cogent is still unexposed and will have conditions suit here. There will be a strong headwind, and there's a bunch of front runners. He'll be able to pick them up late.

Race 1 at Haydock today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 3-year-olds over 1,006 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old gelding Im Next from the Tim Easterby yard, and will be ridden by David Allan. This son of Ardad has constantly shown improvement in his 6 starts to date and certainly caught the eye in his latest when winning his 2nd. He is in with a bright chance in this open-looking race.
Al Hussar, a 3-year-old gelding, ran well at Redcar in its latest run. Dropped a pound and is now looking well handicapped. Each way bet.

Mission Command might be worth one more chance. Wasn't at best form last time out but the slow start really didn't help, he was always on the backfoot after that , he's better than that. His two previous wins did come at today's distance of 5f , he has proven himself capable at Class 4 level and good ground suits. It wouldn't be a surprise to see this horse bounce back with a better effort than he showed last time. Very small each-way tip.

Still Green for Newbury Maiden win when hanging left under pressure but getting up to win by a head. Solid run last time out when 2nd to the promising Gosden horse Bowmark. They won that race with Lead Artist last season, who went on to win two Group 3s and the G1 Lockinge this season. This year's winner probably isn't up to that level; however, subsequently finished 6.5L 14th in the French Derby at 12/1, so they obviously think he's smart, also had an entry in the St James's Palace Stakes. He'd made all that day where nothing else really got involved, and the 3rd was a further 4L behind Point Of Contact. Whoever goes forward will have more competition this day with Tattie Bogle, Sea Baaeed, and We Dare To Dream all liking to be prominent. Haydock is very difficult for front runners, so should suit this one and appeals as the type to win one of these before progressing into the better weekend handicaps.

We Dare to Dream is proving consistent in results, placing in all starts, and can handle ground conditions well. Out of Dark Angel and coming from a yard with an 18% strike rate at Haydock. D Tudhope also has a 16% strike rate for this stable, which is encouraging. E/W possibilities.

Sea Baaeed finished a fair 6th of 13 in the Class 3 King Power Handicap at Leicester. The form of that race has been well advertised with three winners and a second coming out of the race next time around. Richard Hughes steps him up in trip for only his second race in handicaps, and off an unchanged mark, he can remain competitive.

Racing off bottom weight today for this in-form stable with the stable number 1 jockey on board, this horse catches my eye. As does the step up to 7f today, and his previous form indicates a big race is a distinct possibility. Lots of scope up to 7f and receiving weight all around looks like one of the more likely winners.

Three wins and three places from nine career starts. Got up late to take the spoils last time out at Doncaster over today's trip with three of today's rivals behind. Looks a big player here from a favorable draw in stall three.

Ran a solid race at Royal Ascot at big odds when around 5 lengths 6th to Merchant. The form of that run was franked by the second finishing runner-up in the Irish Derby. The form of his two previous races (finished 3rd and 1st) has also been franked, and he could be a potential pattern horse in handicap company. He can reach at least the places for his in-form stable.
With Valiancy taking a huge jump in class and Many Men penalized for a recent win, preference is for Pole Star, who was thereabouts in a Class 2 last time and gets an extra 1lb relief today.
Thrown in at the deep end so far, this horse looks of real interest in this company and the handicap mark isn't too stiff. Expect better than the odds suggest.

One of interest in a very strong race. Tracked this horse for a while and looks to have potential, one of the last of Galileo's crop. Unfortunately, hasn't managed to amount to as much as I'd have hoped. Now taking a step up in trip to 1m6f, previously placed off 1m4f at this track. The pedigree wouldn't normally scream for these longer distances, but his full brother, who was a flat swapped to jump, stays 2 miles comfortably, so perhaps the longer distances could be of ease for this one. Could well be out of its depth in this field of competition with only really making efforts in class 4 & 5. Could still be worth a chance over this longer trip with a good record for a flat galloping track which will suit. Burke's yard is in flying form, hasn't got the most confident of jockey bookings but in hope of a big run with this one over the distance, or if we possibly see this horse swap to jumps like his brother.

Two runs from the 5yo this year. Beaten just a length over 5f last time out in a 13 runner contest, staying on strong from well off the pace. That form looks decent and he’ll be more suited by this 6f trip. He ran some nice races last year while rated about 8lb higher than his current mark. He’ll be fresh after a 2 month break.

Raced as if something was amiss over 7 furlongs at Doncaster last time out when sent off second favourite but finished last of 10. Upset in the stalls that day, which possibly confirms something wasn’t right and could go well off the same mark and dropping back to 6 furlongs.

Lightly raced 5yo. Two runs in the US during the spring and back from a 3 month break with a big run at Royal Ascot for his new UK trainer. He was 4th of 30 runners that day, 2nd of 17 on his side of the track. Two big positives is that he’s a previous C/D winner and he now has top jockey Ryan Moore taking over in the saddle.

Runner-up in both the Palace House and the Temple Stakes in two starts so far this season. Only beaten by a half-length at Haydock last time and has strong claims here, dropping to a Group Three and with a favorable low draw.
Won a Class 2 event in a field of 24 runners last time out at Ascot. Oisin Murphy rides again. 4 places on offer. Hopefully she's bang there again. 6/1

I was drawn to Adrestia stepping up in class here, given her 2yo effort over course and distance would have been competitive on the clock in all bar Battaash’s winning renewal of this, of the races run on Gf ground. She cantered all over them there, but perhaps the pace just set up for her. She’ll need the luck, as many will, but along the same form lines, Queen All Star looks a bit more kindly treated on these terms. She was well on top of Redorange over course and distance last time, and that horse has since come out to chase home Adrestia giving away 6lbs, so the level weights of this pair swing the form slightly in favor of the Channon filly, who is a much bigger price. She’ll be a hostage to fortune from stall 1 if she doesn’t break well, but with a pedigree for further, I hope she can be well in there late on and looks worth her chance on that form line despite having work to do on ratings.

Four career runs from the 3yo filly. She was 2nd of 25 at Royal Ascot in handicap company and 1st of 21 of the runners racing up the centre. She travelled well, hit the line strong, clear of the rest up the centre, and was unlucky to be beaten by one on the far side. Top trainer who can get more improvement from her, strong jockey change, and she should have every chance at this Listed level.

Miss Tonnerre takes a drop in class here, having run in the Musidora last time, which she found much too hot and much too far. That said, she was there pitching at the mile marker, and the horses ahead of her have done plenty for that race since. Notably, all the runners ahead of her were coming into that with at least a run, so I think you can expect her to improve for the run. She’s got one of the best mile efforts on show with her 4th in the May Hill behind the subsequent 1000 Guineas 1-2 in Desert Flower and Flight, with January and Ecstatic doing plenty for the form since too. Officially at the top of these on ratings, I think she is fairly overpriced here in a race that should have a fair enough pace, and she should be a strong stayer at a mile.

Victory Queen has done just enough in two starts so far but comes here a little unexposed for Godolphin and trainer Charlie Appleby (SR 37%). Two wins from two runs so far, both in Class 2 novices in April at Newmarket and Ascot, each over 1 mile. William Buick rode on both occasions and is aboard again here. Kingman filly, a half sister on the dam side to the very smart Group 1 winning Coroebus (died at age 3 having won the St James Palace Stakes). Likely to have progressed at home since the two wins in novice company. Might offer a little value at 7-1.

Unbeaten in 2 runs, and this is another step up in class, but should be capable of placing. Charlie Johnson's journeys to Sandown have not been fruitful so far, but I have a feeling this one will go well.
A course and distance winner last time out and racing off bottom weight can use the weight allowance to good advantage here.
Not too good of late, but his breeding suggests this trip may be ideal. The claimer takes seven pounds off and has shown glimpses of ability. He could go close today.

Arctic Grey looked on an upward curve before the Britannia at Ascot, and he beat the progressive Fort George at Goodwood before that race. He travelled really nicely in the Britannia, but his run was impeded just as he was getting going, and he was eased off to finish 2nd last, which doesn't reflect his ability. He can prove that running all wrong and go close here.

Hotazhell seems a crazy price for this, albeit very competitive looking Group 1 Eclipse. His form matches up with anything else in the race and he should come on for his 4 length third behind Field of Gold in the Irish 2000 Guineas first time out. The ground may be a concern, but he is by Too Darn Hot who's progeny seem to act very well on good to firm ground. His rating of 117, with the weight he gets from the 4 year olds, means he is rated only 1lb behind the odds on favourite Ombudsman, who may have been flattered by his win at Royal Ascot.
Although making its debut today, don't discount this one's chances. The stable is in good nick at the moment and won this race last year, so it could be a nice start to the day.
Karmology showed at Ponte last time that she still retains ability at this level, and I'm hoping she can build on that here.
The trainer is firing in the winners over the last fortnight, so no worries about the form, etc. Has won over this trip 3 times previously and is the stable's only runner here this afternoon.
Another stable that has hit a red-hot streak of form. A winner twice over the distance previously and is the trainer's only representative here today.
Dolly's Delight recently ran well at Doncaster in June but gave the impression a slightly longer distance and uphill finish would suit. She has early pace and can win this one.

I'm going to go win only on this horse since she's likely to put in an all-or-nothing performance, with the hope for the former being partially due to the switch to a stable that does well with these types. The horse hasn't shown much on the racecourse in her 4 runs, in truth, but was sent off just 5/2 in a maiden on debut (finished 6th of 10). The fact she was sent off so short and the fact that the race was stacked with several horses in the 80-90 rating bracket makes me think that she's worth chancing with here off just 52. The shrewd trainer tries a headgear combo for the first time, and he's booked a jockey who has over a 20% strike rate at this tricky track in the last year.

5f nursery winner last summer and made a commendable return after an 8 month break, finishing 2nd out of 9 in a handicap at Thirsk just 18 days ago, even though she wasn't at her best. This performance was promising, and with her stable currently thriving and the in-form Jack Mitchell aboard, she is expected to improve on that effort here.

Narrowly beaten on 4 starts this term but has run into a few issues on those runs, finding itself short of space but always finishing strongly. Jockey now switched out to David Egan, who's not a common booking for this yard but producing 1 win, 2 seconds, and 2 fourths from 13 runs. He's fairly consistent at this course with a 19% strike rate. Trainer also holds a moderate strike rate here, and form has been franked on recent occasions with other close finishers going on to score again.

Ivan Furtado sends just the one horse up to Beverley this afternoon. The Nottinghamshire-based trainer could have gone to Nottingham with Alfa Sea Breeze this afternoon, who was well beaten last time out. But he actually ran a better race than the bare result suggests. He tried to make all over 7 furlongs against Remmooz (4th in Jersey Stakes), fading out of contention 2 furlongs from the line. He has now qualified for handicaps and gets an opening mark of just 60. Dropped in both distance and class, one suspects he will have a much better chance today and provide local owners, Alfa Site Services, with a successful day.

Won over this trip in August 2024 off a mark of 80 in Class 4 and races off 72 in this Class 5. Going okay until weakening inside the final furlong off a mark of 75 in Class 4 company at Ayr last time out and makes his first appearance following recent wind surgery.
Remains the one to beat here, still on a workable mark. Suited by this fast ground, and the trainer is in form currently. Concise again.

Despite being 1 from 16, looks to have clicked back into form since swapping yards with two solid efforts on the all-weather. Now takes the swap back to turf on faster ground. Given its previous form in 2024, he's proven on the ground and distance and should take well to this again. Now with a tumbling mark running off 65 with his sole win coming off 71, a first-time tongue tie could bring on further improvement. First-time booking of highly respected Jack Doughty, previously scoring on his only ride for the yard. Very small yard who have only produced 15 runs this season, but from those efforts have achieved 2 winners and 5 places, so could hold some each-way value with this against a strong favorite in the market who looks similarly rated in my eyes.

Sansanetti looked like a different horse when raised in distance last time winning at 25 to 1. This is a nice race to try and double down as the mark is still generous. 6lb rise will not be enough to slow this one down in my view.

I was at Carlisle when Gullane Girl made her debut in a very valuable novice race in June. She looked a picture and behaved impeccably for a filly having her first sight of a racecourse. She was well held in fourth, behind three decent sorts who had shown a strong level of form between them. I'm surprised she is in a seller; however, it's one of considerable value. I could be wrong, but I think she will go very well after her initial experience and looks way overpriced at 15/2.
Yermanthere looks the pick of Joanna Mason's rides here. She can get a win here after finishing second in a competitive-looking race over course and distance just 10 days ago.

Spirit Genie hasn't threatened the judge so far this season, but he's been up against it in better class races than this. He's also not encountered the soft conditions he relishes. The going will be on the soft side for this race, and I think he could capitalize on that here. Jenny Candlish has had quite a few winners lately, highlighting her string's well-being.

Difficult to ignore off this mark and with such a good record at Carlisle and at this time of the year. Gets on well with this jockey too, and the race distance looks about right. Should go close to winning.

Different Drum ran well at Pontefract on the 9th of June, going down in 4th. The winner set a decent time for the grade. This doesn't look like a very strong race at Carlisle, with the majority of these coming off the back of hurdle races. 15/2 and 3 places.
Wheres The Crumpet looks the one to beat here. In consistent form, winning last time out also. Go close again if staying in this form.

Has a good chance in this. Dropped a pound and jockey claiming another 5lb. He was sent off favorite over course and distance here on penultimate start, shaping well having had to challenge on unfavored side. Each way chance.

Catton Lady looks like a filly who has started to really understand what's required of her, and looks likely to continue on her upward curve. Her victory over Blufferonthebus last time looks good form, given what the second had done since. I think she should be able to defy the minimal rise in the ratings for her win.

Looks like the ideal trip/setup for this one to get his head back in front. Handles this ground and has the experience for a big run in this small field. If he breaks cleanly and gets cover, he will be hard to beat.

In-form trainer Warren Greatrex sends just the one runner to Notts In The City, with his son Ed in the saddle. The 3-year-old Showcasing gelding has progressed with every run, and it is only a matter of time before he gets his head in front. He sets the standard here with a mark of 77, and a big run is expected.

Backing Cushty, the lightly raced 3-year-old Coulsty filly trained by Ruth Carr, in tomorrow’s N & L Franklin Groundworks Handicap over around 1m 2f 50y at Nottingham. She arrives off a solid effort at Ripon on 18 June, when she finished a respectable third of seven over 1m 1f??'tracking the pace before keeping on under James Sullivan . That run followed a tweak back in trip at Redcar on 27 May, where she was seventh of ten, but she bounced back well, showing an obvious fitness edge and returning to form after earlier underwhelming seasonal runs .
Rated around 58, she is running off a modest mark and looks handicapped to strike, especially as she continues to sharpen with each outing. Nottingham’s summer course??'with its straight mile and fair draw bias??'should suit a filly proven over testing trips. Although lightly exposed with just nine starts, Cushty’s recent Ripon third confirms improvement, making her strong each-way value

My vote to take this class 6 handicap will be going to Space Raider a gelded son of Ardad & Bikini ( Dam's sire Trans Island ) who was last seen at Windsor 26 days ago where finishing a creditable 5th/10 currently operating on a mark of 59 I Furtado's inmate has been given a big chance by the handicapper here and he can make the most of such a good opportunity jockey Jordan Nason takes off a handy 3lb which only enhances his good looking claims in what is a straightforward assignment for Space Raider and a good analysis of this class 6 handicap clearly shows Space Raider will be well suited in running here given the horses enrolled to run here must be taken extremely seriously with the handicapper having eased his grip on an individual who is very well capable of better than a mark of 59 in my point of view considered

Followers of breeding would know that this horse is incredibly well-bred and could well be much better than this mark of 75 after pulling hard on seasonal debut last time out off a 2 lb higher mark. He'll strip fitter now, and the stable have hit a real purple patch now too, so it should be all systems go here. The 3rd of 11 in a novice race last year is a piece of form which highlights a strong case for him here since the front 2 are mid-80s type horses, and the 4th and 5th both won their next races to give that form a strong look to it.

Backing Heaven Knows, the lightly raced 3-year-old Showcasing filly trained by Rae Guest, in tomorrow’s Joy Silvester Barbering Handicap (6f 18y). She’s in excellent nick, having won at Chelmsford on her seasonal debut on 8 May, her first start since a long winter break, before following up with a solid fourth of 11 in a competitive handicap at Windsor on 2 June ([source] ). That return to turf confirmed her fitness and ability, showing she adapts well between AW and turf.
Rated around 72, she’s up in class now but continues to thrive fresh and seems straight-fit after that Windsor run. Nottingham’s galloping 6f track??'with a sharp home turn and fair draw bias??'should suit her balanced racing style, especially if she can break smoothly.

5lb claimer for this one, but struggled in handicap debut LTO when 7 of 10 at Goodwood last month. Tricky starting mark, to be fair, so 5lb claimer makes things interesting considering mark remains unchanged.

G M Lyons as a trainer has had his stable in great form of late with 6 wins from just 23 outings inside the last couple of weeks for a 26% win rate. So this looks like a very interesting debutant here.
Tornado Kiss could be a precocious filly who could be showing speed like her sire Acclamation, giving a good account from stall ten on good ground.
Looks to have every chance of winning this. Distance and ground look ideal. G Elliot has a 24% strike rate here at Bellewstown. Came 3rd at Ballinrobe. Yard won this race last year. Chance.

Jack Cleary was not hard on the colt when winning at Gowran Park, with the son of Wootton Bassett staying on strongly at the finish. Wayne Lordon can be following up with another positive show from this progressive-looking colt.

Looking for value in this small field, and Green Soul looks a decent e/w chance here. Won last time out at Fairyhouse and will handle ground conditions well. Top yard and jockey who work well together. E/w chance.
Won very comfortably at Gowran Park on her handicap debut last time out. Can follow up here despite the 12 lbs increase.

MISCHIEF MAN shaped with some promise on his recent handicap debut and Naas's stiff track with today's slightly longer trip should unlock further progress. He was spotted putting in plenty of late work after the line when ridden from the rear that day , and with connections now knowing more representing a powerful yard kept to his own age group he could be the answer.

It's a very open looking race this, Lisnadill is an interesting looking runner. Ran well in defeat over a shorter distance last time out, slow start from the stalls didn't help , she then made up good ground and kept on well late on, she now takes a small step up in trip which could be much more suitable. Lightly raced and probably open to improvement, ground conditions ideal.

Encosta is progressing steadily and ran well when he was an unlucky second behind Sonnyboyliston at Listowel at the end of May. Given time to recover, today is a fair opportunity for Encosta to step forward. With Noel Meade in form, we trust him with our NAP.

Avondale is returning to hurdling, and Barry Connell could be rewarded with a good run appearing. Avondale was last seen winning on the flat over twelve furlongs at Galway and Roscommon. He has speed and stamina, which can make him a formidable force here with Sean Flanagan achieving success.

I have lost track of the number of trainers El Bello has had over the years, but he is currently with Denis Hogan, for whom he had his third and latest win over seven furlongs at Dundalk last year. He could defy top weight because he has won five times on the flat and is making his hurdling debut here. He has an e.w. chance.

John McConnel's mare, who is by Court Cave, was third over hurdles at Limerick, beaten nine lengths by Emily Love. Dylan Kid was in the plate that day. Today, Alex Harvey has the ride, and he takes off five pounds. She could be making up the nine lengths she was beaten by and hopefully win by this distance. That sees her racing over a slightly longer trip that can play to her stamina strengths.

A Pinatubo filly, a half-sister to the 14.5f winner Rain. She sports cheekpieces and in a barrier trial at Naas in May, she placed 5th among 9, suggesting she could be in contention for a top finish, which makes her a worthwhile each-way wager at 25/1.
Good up and coming jockey booked. Horse has been showing a nice bit of form recently and off a nice mark today. Must go close in this.

Hell Left Loose ran well last time when 3rd at Limerick over 7f. The nine-year-old still has a bit of life left in him. Drawn in stall 19 of the 19 runners, he could aim to be involved in the finish on the stands side rail over 6f. With the top 3 in the betting drawn 15, 13, and 12, the pace will be on the stands side. Hell Left Loose has a mark of only 40, with Nicola Burns taking off a further four pounds.
Stable in good form, picking up 2 winners yesterday and going close with this horse when attempting to land a gamble. Could outrun current odds if turned out again 24 hours later.
In fine form prior to below par effort last time out. Back to last winning mark and the stiff track should suit him here today. One to watch.

Noble Name needs a change of luck. She won a point and was a decent 3rd in her first bumper, and then was held up at Downpatrick but got tightened up on the bend and slipped up in her latest race. She could go close against previous winners, getting weight from them.

In receipt of plenty of weight for a rematch with Gazelle D'or when going down by that rival by a length, with the aforementioned winning again. This lightly raced horse looks well-weighted to gain its first career success. NAP

Gazelle D'Or stormed home last time when switched to 5f. Jack Cleary, claiming 5lbs today, has already steered the selection to win two races. The draw doesn't look like it will cause an issue, so I am good with this at 5.5.

Stuntman Steve has been ultra consistent and got a deserved win when showing a good attitude to win when having to be pushed along some way out on the last run. The rider's claim negates the 5lb penalty for that win and is my preference ahead of the stablemate and current favorite for the race.

Should Emmet Mullins' newest yard member, the 5-year-old gelding TOLL STONE be ready to fire first time out, this son of AUSTRALIA must be there or thereabouts. Fitness is a question returning from a 230-day absence, but he has defied a long layoff before - winning at Galway after 123 days off. His last three runs show strong form, including a fine 7th in a Class 1 Premier Handicap at Cheltenham, just half a length behind Fiercely Proud, who won a premier handicap at Ascot next time. He also had Cracking Rhapsody and Teddy Blue behind him, both of whom have run well since.
Donagh Meyler takes the ride - he's in good form and holds a 40% strike rate at Bellewstown over the past year. Mullins also has a 30.77% place strike rate with runners off long layoffs, which adds to confidence.
At 16/1, with five places on offer, there's more than enough in Toll Stone's profile to justify a play - if he’s fit and ready. Given his past form and connections, he looks overpriced and could outrun those odds. A speculative but worthwhile each-way punt in a competitive field.

Quickened had the run of the race at a sharp track, slightly fortunate due to a late faller. Scored by three and a quarter lengths off 110 over 2m4f at Killarney three starts back. Top jockey back on board. Good mark on penultimate run. Should be in the mix each way.

Hasten Slowly will not be hanging around with the mare forcing the pace and pray that Alex Harvey can get the fractions right to be successful. She can be a clean hurdler, and with Alex Harvey taking off five pounds, I can see her being in the equation at the finish.
Garnacho comes into this one today after a break of six months. He had a third on the last run. Price and five places say good for each way.

The Border Boy reached the placings for the first time when 4th in his latest race, having fallen to a low mark of 74. The handicapper has dropped him another pound. In this opportunity handicap hurdle, Danny Power rides over hurdles for the second time, having ridden at Wexford yesterday, taking off another four pounds to a weight of nine stone eleven pounds. He has previously ridden only on the flat with one win from 26 rides, only two of which were this year.

GLENS SENSATION could be interesting starting out life in handicap company from a lowly mark. He may have previously had his issues low-mileage for his age , but may have been prepared for his debut in this sphere to land some bets and the post-time market could tell us more.

Adrian Sexton's 5 year old Mare SHING SHILLA gets a ride here today from First Reserve & looking back at this Daughter of GLENEAGLE's penultimate run at Ballinrobe (22f) where this Mare was bang there for the majority of the contest, only fading 2 out from the finish. Forced paced tactics certainly didn't do that trick last time out over 22f at Tramore so she looks intriguing now dropping down to 20f, Dropped 2lbs & gets a more experienced jockey in the shape of Harry Sexton (4lbs Claimer) who takes the reins for his father. This charge could be ready to go this time with a bit more of a break (was thrust right back into action just 3 days removed last time out) now dropping in trip. 5 places & enough of a price for me to toss a penny into the well & hope.
Jaadil is an interesting runner here who could make the places. Badly hampered last time out and this step up in trip will suit. One to watch.
